title: Add contextual log mosaic and token-lattice dashboard for low-latency debugging
author: Asha Raman
description:
Motivation: debugging low-latency, token-level quality regressions is frequently manual and slow — engineers need a single-pane view that correlates token-phase timing, per-token cost, and contextual log snippets to reduce time-to-blame. This PR introduces a Contextual Log Mosaic (a compact log-sample heatmap aligned to token-phase spans) and a Token Lattice dashboard (token-phase timing + cost signatures with cohort filtering), plus small infra hooks to emit short-lived trace anchors for sampled invocations. Changes include dashboard JSON, two new dashboard panels, a lightweight trace hook library used by the sampler, and a small opt-in sampling toggle.

What this delivers (single continuous description): Add two Grafana dashboards under observability/dashboards: "Contextual Log Mosaic" and "Token Lattice Explorer"; instrumented a new lightweight span anchor API (invocation.anchor_trace) that emits compact token-phase boundaries (start/end timestamps per-phase) and a log sample pointer; added a sampled-log fuzzy-join helper that approximates join keys when logs arrive out of order; introduced a small config flag (OBS_CONTEXTUAL_SAMPLER=true) to opt-in to the richer sampling stream; added backfill migration for 14 days of synthetic anchors for existing sampled traces to bootstrap dashboards. Rationale: the mosaic dashboard surfaces per-invocation rows with a compact mosaic of token-phase buckets (input, encode, kv-lookup, decode) where color intensity maps to median token-latency and an overlay sparkline shows token-cost deltas; the lattice lets engineers slice by prompt-shape, model, and tenant and inspect the 95th and 99th percentile token-phase durations alongside per-token cost attribution. The trace anchors enable cheap correlation between span timing and the actual logs without retaining full request logs for every invocation.

Checklist:
- [x] Dashboard JSONs added and validated with local Grafana preview
- [x] Instrumentation library added (lightweight, <2KB payload per anchor)
- [x] E2E smoke test for sampling toggle
- [x] Backfill migration script and one-off run logs attached
- [x] Docs: short runbook added to docs/observability/ (how to use dashboards and how to interpret colors)
- [x] Security review: no PII emitted by anchor payloads (only stable hashes and offsets)

Files changed (high level): ["dashboards/contextual_log_mosaic.json", "dashboards/token_lattice.json", "runtime/trace_anchor.go", "observability/sampler.go", "observability/sampler_test.go", "migrations/20241102_backfill_anchors.sql", "docs/observability/contextual_mosaic.md", "pkg/logjoin/fuzzy_join.go", "pkg/logjoin/fuzzy_join_test.go"]

Small illustrative snippet (in description only): invocation.anchor_trace emits a compact proto: {invocation_id_hash, tenant_id_hash, phases: [(name, start_ms, end_ms, token_count)], log_pointer: (bucket_id, offset)} — no raw user content. The fuzzy_join uses stable 8-byte anchors and a short TTL to join logs arriving up to 30s late.

Review conversation (summary as one continuous string): "Priya: Please ensure the anchor payload doesn't contain raw prompt text; can we include a verification test?" "Asha: added test fuzzy_join_test.go and asserted no prompt content; payload only includes stable hashes and numeric offsets; added security note in docs." "Jonah: Dashboard looks good; request to surface 'kernel-wait' as a separate phase in the lattice — prefer as opt-in because not all kernels emit it." "Asha: made kernel-wait an optional phase (configurable via tracer_phase_config), updated dashboard to hide empty columns by default." "Erin: CI flaked on migration run; reran and green; lgtm from SRE after reducing backfill IO pressure." "Merge: squashed and merged after approvals from Priya and Jonah."

CI summary: ["lint: pass", "unit: pass (observability unit tests)", "integration: pass (sampler smoke)", "dashboard-validate: pass (grafana-lint)", "migration-test: pass after rerun"]

Manual testing notes: Bootstrapped a staging run against a sampled tenant; used 'Token Lattice Explorer' to find a 99th-percentile decode-phase spike; correlated to mosaic row and identified KV-cache miss followed by long kernel-wait on an older CUDA kernel; fix tracked in ENG-2360.

Migration and rollout: Backfill script run in staging and a small pilot tenant in production to verify IO impact (peak additional DB writes ~2.8% on sampled shard). Rollout plan: enable OBS_CONTEXTUAL_SAMPLER for 5% of sampled traffic, monitor write amplification and latency SLOs for 48h, then increase to 25% if stable.

Follow-ups: add a compact UI inspector for the anchor payload and add support for exporting lattice cohorts to CSV (follow-up ENG-2371).

release_notes: Add two observability dashboards: Contextual Log Mosaic and Token Lattice Explorer; lightweight trace anchors for token-phase correlation; opt-in sampling toggle OBS_CONTEXTUAL_SAMPLER; backfill script to bootstrap anchors. Improves investigation time for token-phase regressions and reduces manual log joins.
usage_examples: Open Grafana > Contextual Log Mosaic > filter by tenant and prompt-shape; click a row to jump to the trace in Trace UI
Open Token Lattice Explorer > set cohort filter (model, prompt length) and inspect 95/99p phase durations; hover tokens to see cost deltas
notes_security_privacy: Anchor payloads contain only stable hashes, numeric offsets, phase times, and a log pointer. No PII or prompt text is emitted. Security review completed and documented in docs/observability/contextual_mosaic.md.
